claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.text: I have one child - Alex is 7 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to understand the rules properly. Let me read the official guidance first.

Good, I have the eligibility information. Now let me ask you some key questions to determine if you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**First question: Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

**Which country are you currently living in?**

conversation.text: I'm living in Spain at the moment.

Let me ask you this:

**Are you a Crown servant (such as a member of the UK Armed Forces or UK civil service posted abroad)?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me so far, let me confirm the current situation:

- You live in Spain (not the UK)
- You're not a Crown servant
- You don't have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can only claim Child Benefit if you live abroad in certain specific circumstances, such as being a Crown servant or having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme. Since neither of these applies to you, I'm unable to assess your eligibility as eligible for Child Benefit.

However, before I provide my final decision, let me ask one more clarifying question to be thorough:

**Are you a family member of an EEA or Swiss national who has a right to reside in the UK, and are you claiming based on that relationship?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

## Summary

**You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

The main reason is that Child Benefit eligibility requires you to be living in the UK. While you have a child (Alex, age 7) who would normally qualify, the fact that you are currently living in Spain means you don't meet the basic residency requirement.

The only exceptions that would allow you to claim while living abroad are:
- Being a Crown servant
- Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with certain conditions)
- Being a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with the right to reside

Since none of these apply to your situation, you cannot claim Child Benefit at this time. If you move back to the UK in the future, you would then be able to apply for Child Benefit for Alex.
